hook.line: Plans move all the time, and in Bogotá probably more than most. When Mariana has to shift a meeting, three or four verbs do the work.
hook.es: Adelantamos la reunión para el lunes.
hook.en: We brought the meeting forward to Monday.

examples.es: Adelantamos la reunión para el lunes.
examples.en: We brought the meeting forward to Monday.
We have to postpone the trip.

examples.es: ¿Podemos correr la cita para las cuatro?
examples.en: Can we move the appointment to four o'clock?

examples.es: Aplazaron la fiesta para la próxima semana.
examples.en: They postponed the party until next week.

examples.es: Vale adelantó el pedido para el viernes.
examples.en: Vale brought the order forward to Friday.

examples.es: Quiero posponer la clase para mañana.
examples.en: I want to postpone the class until tomorrow.

rule:
The direction is inside the verb. *Adelantar* moves something earlier. *Aplazar* and *posponer* move it later. *Correr* is the everyday Colombian way to say "move" either way: *correr la cita*.

The thing you move is the object: *la reunión*, *el viaje*. The new date comes after *para*: *para el lunes*.

English needs "bring forward", "push back", "put off". Spanish just picks one verb.
smallPrint: Teachers call *para* here a preposition of deadline: it marks the date something is set for.

readAndPick.es: Adelantamos la reunión para el lunes.
options: We postponed the meeting to Monday.
We brought the meeting forward to Monday.
We cancelled the meeting on Monday.
They brought the trip forward to December.
They planned the trip for December.
They postponed the trip until December.

readAndPick.es: ¿Podemos correr la cita para las cuatro?
options: Can we move the appointment to four o'clock?
Can we cancel the appointment at four?
Did we miss the appointment at four?
I'm going to bring the class forward.
I'm going to postpone the class.
I'm going to teach the class.
We have to bring the visit forward.
We have to make the visit.
We have to postpone the visit.

readAndPick.es: Adelantaron el vuelo para el martes.
options: They brought the flight forward to Tuesday.
They postponed the flight until Tuesday.
They took the flight on Tuesday.

readAndPick.es: Posponemos la fiesta para el sábado.
options: We're bringing the party forward to Saturday.
We held the party on Saturday.
We're postponing the party until Saturday.
I want to postpone the appointment.
I want to bring the appointment forward.
I want to forget the appointment.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *___ la reunión para el lunes.* (*Adelantamos* or *Aplazamos*) We brought the meeting forward to Monday.
yourTurn.answer: Adelantamos la reunión para el lunes.
yourTurn.why: *Adelantar* means earlier, and Monday comes sooner.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Aplazaron el viaje ___ diciembre.* (*para* or *a*) They postponed the trip until December.

yourTurn.why: *Aplazar* moves it later, and the trip is the object.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a colleague: Can we move the appointment to four o'clock?
yourTurn.answer: ¿Podemos correr la cita para las cuatro?
accept: ¿Podemos adelantar la cita para las cuatro?
¿Podemos aplazar la cita para las cuatro?
yourTurn.why: *Correr la cita* means move it, and the new time follows *para*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Vale brought the order forward to Friday.
yourTurn.answer: Vale adelantó el pedido para el viernes.
yourTurn.why: *Adelantó* is the *she* form, and the new date follows *para*.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn it around so it is later: *Adelantamos la reunión.*
Make it about *they*: *Adelantamos el vuelo para el martes.*
yourTurn.answer: Adelantaron el vuelo para el martes.

pitfalls.wrong: Adelantamos la reunión para más tarde.
pitfalls.right: Aplazamos la reunión para más tarde.
pitfalls.why: *Adelantar* always means earlier. For later, use *aplazar* or *posponer*.

pitfalls.wrong: Aplazamos la reunión en el lunes.
pitfalls.right: Aplazamos la reunión para el lunes.
pitfalls.why: The new date after these verbs comes with *para*, not *en*.
The thing you move is the object, with no *para*. Use *para* only for the new date.

personal: Think of something you keep putting off and say it: *Quiero aplazar…* or *Voy a posponer…*, and when you will do it with *para*.
